hypotheses.mechanism: Checkout service version 1.9.0 introduced a bug in the payment routing logic that causes high error rates when interacting with payment-svc

cause.statement: Checkout service version 1.9.0 (build b-1245) was deployed with a change to payment routing

runtime_effect.statement: Checkout service starts routing requests to payment-svc through a new sidecar port that is unstable

symptom.statement: Checkout service error rate exceeds 10% for 15 seconds

hypotheses.mechanism: Payment service version 2.4.2 introduced a regression in handling checkout requests that causes high error rates

cause.statement: Payment service version 2.4.2 (build b-1246) was deployed with a new feature

runtime_effect.statement: Payment service becomes unresponsive to checkout requests due to new feature

symptom.statement: Checkout service error rate exceeds 10% for 15 seconds

hypotheses.mechanism: Checkout service's error rate metric is misconfigured, causing false positives in the alert

cause.statement: Checkout service error rate metric was misconfigured in the alert rule

runtime_effect.statement: Error rate metric incorrectly reports high error rates

symptom.statement: Checkout service error rate exceeds 10% for 15 seconds

parsed.rationale: The checkout-svc error rate metric shows a sudden spike to 100% starting at 06:59:39, which aligns with the deployment of checkout-svc v1.9.0 (build b-1245) that introduced a change to route payments through a new sidecar port. The commit message for this change (commit:e8d58bd) explicitly states the new routing mechanism, and the error rate metric (metric:17df7c1b11) confirms the spike. No contradicting evidence exists for this hypothesis.
